title: source files are LF on every box, so a seal's fingerprint means the same bytes everywhere
intention: cairn/.gitattributes pins *.py, *.md and *.txt to eol=lf, so a checkout holds the same bytes on every box and a seal's fingerprint means the same bytes everywhere; git add --renormalize in the build commit, which is empty because the blobs are already LF.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: bce4 closure fingerprint: CRLF checkout a614f1bf0b613043ab34a79d1441e065ca80e0426df639f70ee6e670783ddae5, *.py eol=lf checkout 9236ec0db64b7ad018656610854360ff20e922cc314800e238f51e09374c2612 (equals the Linux value the orchestrator holds)
traces_to: Law 3: a fingerprint is a measurement and has to mean the same bytes on every box; Law 4: the line ending is enforced by git's attributes, not by a reader remembering.
how: Add `*.py text eol=lf`, `*.md text eol=lf` and `*.txt text eol=lf` to .gitattributes beside the json and sh pins, with a why-comment. Run git add --renormalize on tracked files in the build commit. Proof: copy the repo's real .gitattributes into a scratch git repo and read git check-attr eol for a .py, a .md and a .txt path (eol: lf), and for a .cmd path (crlf, untouched). The fingerprint equality is the measured why, kept in the ticket, not re-asserted by the proof.

clauses.claim: git check-attr eol reads lf for a .py, a .md and a .txt path under the repo's .gitattributes
the pin leaves the .cmd crlf and the existing json/sh pins as they were

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

measured.saw: bce4 closure fingerprint: CRLF checkout a614f1bf0b613043ab34a79d1441e065ca80e0426df639f70ee6e670783ddae5, *.py eol=lf checkout 9236ec0db64b7ad018656610854360ff20e922cc314800e238f51e09374c2612 (equals the Linux value the orchestrator holds)
measured.how: two fresh --no-checkout clones of cairn HEAD with core.autocrlf=true, one with the pin in .git/info/attributes; ran the proof, captured its closure, hashed with validation_store.source_fingerprint

measured.saw: the index holds every *.py/*.md/*.txt blob as LF: 1068 i/lf w/crlf, 11 i/lf w/lf, 2 i/lf w/mixed, 74 not text
measured.how: git ls-files --eol over the three globs

orient.intent: cairn/.gitattributes pins *.py, *.md and *.txt to eol=lf, so a checkout holds the same bytes on every box and the validation store's fingerprint of a closure is the same on Windows as on Linux; the renormalize in the build commit is empty because the blobs are already LF.
orient.scope: .gitattributes and its proof; the validation store's fingerprint code, the live tree's autocrlf setting and the existing json/sh/cmd pins are not changed
unknowns: a checkout made before the pin stays CRLF until files are re-checked-out; the live tree is not touched here
the posix side was not run by me: on Linux the pin changes nothing a checkout does
